fact_check.claim: Registrar says median grade information is not calculated or made publicly available
fact_check.note: Page says: 'Median grade information is not calculated or made publicly available.' The unsupported 'shares only with deans' sentence from round one was removed (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: Medians went on the registrar's website in 1998 and on transcripts in 2008; Faculty Senate removed them from the website in 2011
fact_check.note: Sun article gives 1998, 2008 and 2011 as stated.

fact_check.claim: Faculty Senate voted May 11, 2011, after concluding online grade information induced students to select leniently graded courses
fact_check.note: Chronicle gives May 11, 2011 and the 'induced students to select leniently graded courses' finding.

fact_check.claim: On Dec. 15, 2023 the Faculty Senate approved a resolution ending median grades on transcripts; courses taken in Fall 2023 and later do not show them
fact_check.note: Sun reports Resolution 193 approved Dec. 15, 2023 and applies to courses from Fall 2023 on; not retroactive.

fact_check.claim: Dean of Faculty archive lists the measure as Resolution 193, 'Discontinue Posting Median Grades on Student Transcripts'
fact_check.note: Page title and number match. The adoption date was not visible in the part of the page that loaded, but the article attributes the date to the Sun, not to this page.

fact_check.claim: Jonah Bernard, a sophomore in the College of Engineering, argued in a January 2024 Guest Room column that without medians students rely on rumors from friends, favoring the well-connected
fact_check.note: Author, class year, college and January 2024 date match; column says medians remove the advantage for well-connected students who hear rumors from friends.

fact_check.claim: Christian Baran, a sophomore in Arts and Sciences, wrote in a Nov 2019 Sun column that students shouldn't load up on unrelated difficult courses but shouldn't hunt for the easiest classes until graduation; oceanography as an example of a class taken out of interest
fact_check.note: Author, year, date and the balance argument match. Oceanography is used as an example of a lighter schedule he won't judge, and he notes many students are truly interested in such courses; the article's paraphrase is close enough.

fact_check.claim: ILR/STSCI 2100 Intro to Statistics: c0rn3lL, Dec 2012, called it the easiest math course anyone can take
fact_check.note: Posted Dec 20, 2012: 'undoubtedly the easiest math course anyone can take at Cornell'.

fact_check.claim: mikeyc765 (2012) said non-math statistics courses have a reputation for being easy
fact_check.note: Dec 4, 2012 post suggests introductory statistics from non-math departments as an option not requiring complex math. 'Reputation for being easy' is a mild stretch but acceptable.

fact_check.claim: ILR statistics: monydad, Jun 2018, likely relatively easy, not sure it is the easiest
fact_check.note: Posted June 25, 2018: 'I have reason to suspect that ILR stats is relatively easy. Whether or not it is actually the easiest.'

fact_check.claim: Psych 101: Brown_man1987, Jul 2008, listed as an easy option
fact_check.note: Thread (July 2008) has Brown_man1987 calling it 'reputed to being one of the easiest classes around'.

fact_check.claim: Sociology 101: Spanks, Jul 2008, listed as an easy option
fact_check.note: Spanks (July 2, 2008) wrote only 'sociology 101' with no difficulty comment. Brown_man1987 then said not to take Soc 101 and to take DSoc 101 instead, as the easier one. The thread does not call Soc 101 easy, and the table's Soc 101 row misattributes it.

fact_check.claim: DSoc 101: Brown_man1987 and AppleMuncher, Jul 2008; Brown_man1987 called it easier than Soc 101
fact_check.note: Brown_man1987 says DSoc 101 is easier than Soc 101 with a median A; AppleMuncher says an A should be easy.

fact_check.claim: Oceanography and Earthquake!: cuapplecider9, not very difficult, fulfilled a science requirement
fact_check.note: Matches the thread.

fact_check.claim: Classic 236, Greek Mythology: Biophilic, easy and fun
fact_check.note: Biophilic calls it easy and fun. The thread writes 'Classics 236'; the article's 'Classic 236' is a minor course-code typo.

fact_check.claim: Climate and Global Warming (EAS 268): laurstar07, called it fun and recommended it for meteorology fans
fact_check.note: laurstar07 calls it fun, especially for meteorology fans. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Same thread also mentions a mushroom class, a dinosaurs class and Ancient Egypt, and one poster warns against Space Exploration without astronomy background
fact_check.note: cuapplecider9 mentions Mushrooms, Dinosaurs, Ancient Egypt, and found Space Exploration hard without astronomy background.

fact_check.claim: Class Roster has a 'Show classes with syllabi only' option and filters for distribution requirements, class level, credits and grade option
fact_check.note: All five filters are present on the roster page.

fact_check.claim: Sun's 2022 iconic fall classes piece and 2018 'best course' Sunspots are not lists of easy classes
fact_check.note: Both pieces were opened; neither lists easy classes (2022 piece calls CHEM 2070 a difficult rite of passage; 2018 picks are praised for instructors and content). The 2018 link is https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2018/10/sunspots-whats-the-best-course-youve-taken-at-cornell.

fact_check.claim: The oldest posts are 18 years old (2008)
fact_check.note: July 2008 to Nov 2026 is 18 years.

beats_top.why: The first result is a scraped-looking page that would not load (DNS failure), and the real student-facing results are old forum threads and a Sun opinion column. Our page answers in the first paragraph that no official list exists and why, dates every claim, and says how to choose.
changes: Fix the Sociology 101 row so it no longer claims it was named as easy.
Optionally add more recent (2020+) student-named courses with links if an openable source exists.

fixes: Delete the 'Sociology 101 | Spanks' table row (Spanks only wrote 'sociology 101' with no difficulty comment, and Brown_man1987 told readers to avoid Soc 101 in favor of DSoc 101; source https://talk.collegeconfidential.com/t/credit-filler-courses/520677), and in the DSoc 101 row keep that Brown_man1987 called it easier than Soc 101. Also change 'Classic 236' to 'Classics 236'. Not applied because this was the second review: a second fix verdict is converted to reject by the pipeline.
